Article Title: 'Mr C Joseph hates Sanatan': BJP hits out at Vijay govt after SC's Deepam rebuke
Article Text:
BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia addressing press conference after SC order of Deepam

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday slammed the Tamil Nadu government after the Supreme Court issued contempt notices to senior state officials over the Karthigai Deepam row, accusing chief minister C Joseph Vijay of deliberately violating constitutional principles and hurting the religious sentiments of Hindu devotees.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also hailed the SC order saying, "A historic victory for every devotee of Lord Murugan! By ordering the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the Thiruparankundram Deepathoon tomorrow and pulling up Tamil Nadu authorities for acting at the dictates of their political bosses, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has thoroughly exposed the INDI Alliance government's anti-Sanatan mindset.""No political conspiracy can stop the sacred traditions of Bharat. May the divine blessings of Lord Murugan protect all devotees and guide them on the path of courage and righteousness," he added.Meanwhile, addressing a press conference, BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia alleged that the controversy had arisen because of the state government's hostility towards Sanatan traditions and the Hindu community."This press conference is being held on a very important issue relating to the Karthigai Deepam row, which has been created only because the government in Tamil Nadu and the chief minister there, Mr C Joseph, hate Sanatan traditions and the Hindu community.This hatred is so deep that a chief minister who has taken an oath to protect and preserve the ethos of the Constitution has, prima facie, wilfully decided to violate it," Bhatia said.BJP leader CR Kesavan also criticised the state government, calling the Supreme Court's direction to light the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon on Saturday a victory for devotees of Lord Muruga."The sacred Karthigai Deepam, which will now be lit at the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill tomorrow, is indeed an emphatic victory and a true triumph for the implicit faith and sentiments of crores of Lord Muruga devotees," Kesavan said.He accused the state government of using the controversy for political gains and alleged that its actions had hurt the sentiments of Hindu devotees."The dubious and dangerous divisive drama enacted and orchestrated by the TVK Congress government to perpetrate their vote-bank politics of communal appeasement deeply hurt and humiliated the sentiments of countless Hindu devotees," he said.Kesavan further demanded an unconditional apology from Vijay, saying, "This TVK Congress government, led by Joseph Vijay needs to tender an unconditional apology immediately to the people of Tamil Nadu and crores of Lord Muruga devotees for betraying their faith."The row centres on the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu's Madurai district. The dispute escalated after the Madras High Court directed that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the pillar, amid objections and competing claims over the site.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted the lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. However, the ceremonial flame was lit only at the customary Uchaipillaiyar mandapam and not at the disputed pillar, prompting contempt proceedings.Then earlier Friday, the Supreme Court directed that the traditional lamp be lit atop Deepathoon on Saturday using the flame lit at the Uchaipillaiyar mandapam. It also issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police, Madurai Collector and other officials over the alleged non-compliance with its earlier order.The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi observed that the state executive authorities appeared to have acted on the "diktats of their political bosses" and said wilful non-compliance with court orders would have to be dealt with an "iron hand".The court also suspended the temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to take over its management, and handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF.
Article Summary: The row centres on the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu's Madurai district. The dispute escalated after the Madras High Court directed that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the pillar, amid objections and competing claims over the site. On Friday, the Supreme Court issued contempt notices to senior state officials over the row.

Article Title: 'DMK supports Constitution': Congress praises ex-ally ahead of special Parliament session

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday heaped praise on the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam ( DMK ) and extended an invitation to the opposition meeting scheduled amid speculation over the Delimitation Bill to be tabled during Parliament’s Special Session.Speaking to reporters, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said that the DMK always stands with the Constitution of India and that whoever loves the Constitution cannot support the Delimitation Bill.“We are approaching everybody. The DMK always stands with the Constitution of India. I think whoever loves the Constitution of India cannot support these types of divisive agendas,” Venugopal said.“So we will approach all the opposition parties,” he added.This comes as INDIA bloc and other opposition parties are scheduled to meet at 11:30 am on Saturday to discuss their strategy and decide on the next course of action.Venugopal alleged that the Centre, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, was trying to set a “big trap” for the people of India, claiming that this was the design behind the entire episode."The government of India, PM Modi and HM Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India.That is the design of this entire episode,” he said.“INDIA alliance and opposition parties will have a meeting tomorrow morning at 11:30. We will make the strategy and take a decision tomorrow morning at 11:30 am,” he added.This comes amid speculation over the DMK's possible position on the delimitation proposals and allegations by the ruling TVK that the party could be moving closer to the BJP-led Centre.The DMK has, however, denied any move towards an alliance with the BJP.Earlier in the day, DMK chief MK Stalin reiterated the party's two demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, insisting that Tamil Nadu 's existing 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests; nor will it depart from its principles," the party chief asserted on the Centre's expected delimitation move."The shameless and ungrateful lot who abandoned their principles for positions of power must realise this," he said, apparently hitting out at the Congress party, which joined the TVK alliance and the government led by it after the DMK was defeated in the assembly polls held earlier this year.
Article Summary: Congress heaped praise on the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam ( DMK ) and extended an invitation to the opposition meeting scheduled amid speculation over the Delimitation Bill to be tabled during Parliament’s Special Session. Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said that the DMK always stands with the Constitution of India.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Friday announced that she would skip the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday to discuss the opposition's floor strategy for the special Parliament session , citing her father and party chief Sharad Pawar 's health.With Sharad Pawar hospitalised, the Baramati MP, will remain in Mumbai over the weekend."I will go to Delhi on Monday morning to attend the session," she wrote in her WhatsApp status, PTI reported.Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration.It remains unclear whether the NCP (SP) will be represented at the meeting and, if so, who will attend on behalf of the party.Sule's announcement came on a day when the NCP (SP) issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30, when the special session is scheduled to begin. NEW DELHI: The younger brother of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee , Swapan Banerjee on Thursday approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee , alleging intimidation and obstruction to a blood donation camp, news agency PTI reported.Swapan, popularly known as Babun, alleged that a culture of threats and intimidation had taken root during the TMC's 15-year rule in the state and continued even after the BJP came to power in May this year. Article Summary: Swapan Banerjee has approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek. Article Title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das
Article Text:
Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.

Can’t give LOC copy as Das yet to respond to Nov 23 notice: Government

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Besides Das, lookout circulars have been issued against CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka over CJP’s protest at Dadar on October 2.Centre’s counsel said Das was free to challenge the circular in the appropriate court, reiterating that the CJP functionary also faces scrutiny for “multiple discrepancies” in his passport that could affect his citizenship.Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport on the day he was to fly to UK.“The LOC is clearly an afterthought,” Das said in a statement later, asking why declared fugitives such as Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi had been allowed to leave the country while activists like him were being stopped.Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.The counsel said enforcement agencies were awaiting the outcome of an inquiry that started in Puducherry to verify Das’s place of birth, address and parentage, pointing out that the passport column meant to have details of his father had been left blank.He said that, assuming passport authorities find Das’s explanation inadequate, he could be “left stranded in no-man’s land”.Additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma and standing counsel Ashish Dixit said a copy of the lookout circular could not be immediately given to Das because he was yet to respond to the show-cause notice issued on Nov 23.That notice, Sharma said, states that inputs were received indicating Das’s place of birth was incorrect and that his passport had been obtained by suppressing facts. “It requires clarification and supporting documents, failing which the passport may be suspended or impounded,” he said.The ASG also told the court that Madras HC issued notice on a plea seeking an inquiry into Das’s antecedents on Oct 30.Sibal countered that a pending show-cause notice over discrepancies could not translate into a travel ban. “There is no revocation, suspension, impounding of the passport. The show-cause notice doesn’t mean necessarily there will be harsh consequences… he will respond to the notice in due course,” he said, arguing that travel was a fundamental right.
Article Summary: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das. The circular was issued at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday rejected a plea seeking the removal of videos showing Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at a Congress-organised event in Hyderabad.The plea had also asked for an independent SIT probe into the participation of foreign delegates and the permissions granted to them for attending the event.During an earlier mentioning before Chief Justic Surya Kant, the petitioner's counsel alleged the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had interfered in India's domestic politics by criticising the government and expressing support for the Opposition.The plea came after Filibeck's remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026, held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14. He had expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress, saying democracy was "under attack" in India and calling for international support to defend it.His use of the slogan, popularised by Rahul Gandhi, drew criticism from the BJP , which accused the Congress of allowing foreign political representatives to comment on India's internal affairs.Filibeck also said the PES, Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy."True democracy. Not the corrupted one, not the rigged one, not the fake one," he said.The Party of European Socialists (PES) is a transnational European political party that brings together socialist, social democratic, and labour parties across Europe.Around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries, were present at The Bharat Summit 2026, which held discussions over geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.
Article Summary: Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raised the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at a Congress-organised event in Hyderabad. The plea had also asked for an independent SIT probe into the participation of foreign delegates.

NEW DELHI: A special sitting of Parliament will begin on November 30, with the government expected to consider reviving its push for a constitutional amendment linking women’s reservation to delimitation. The move could set the stage for a fresh political confrontation with the Opposition.The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with the sittings scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.The government has not officially confirmed which Bills will be taken up. However, speculation has gathered pace over the proposed Delimitation Bill and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026,” Rijiju said in a post on X.The special sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 and subsequently prorogued.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in legislative bodies.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha during the special sitting on April 16-17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, with 11 members abstaining. At the time, the House had 528 members and the Bill needed 352 votes to pass.The draft had not provided for a proportional 50 per cent increase in seats across states, a key concern for regional parties, particularly those from southern India. The government has since explored a formula to increase seats by 50 per cent in every state while retaining the existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.The opposition parties are also expected to carry their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation into Parliament.The BJP leaders are banking on support from the DMK, NCP-SP and breakaway factions of the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena for the delimitation bill. The DMK has 22 Lok Sabha MPs and the NCP (SP) has eight. Both parties have indicated they could consider backing the proposal if their states' share of seats is protected.NCP-SCP MP Supriya Sule on Wednesday said the proposed Delimitation Bill should first be introduced and its full text made available for scrutiny. “Let the bill be introduced first; let us have the full bill in our hands. Once we have it, we can discuss it—and perhaps it will turn out to be a good one,” she told reporters.YSRCP is also expected to support the Delimitation Bill, according to sources quoted by news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Congress and NCP (SP) are stepping up coordination ahead of the sitting, with the parties summoning their MPs to discuss the proposed legislation and the Opposition's strategy.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said the government was hoping to secure its “super-tainted” two-thirds majority. “A fight is on,” he said.The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet at Sewa Teerth in New Delhi at 1 pm on Friday.The meeting comes as the BJP holds a two-day gathering of its national office-bearers and state in-charges at the PUSA campus on November 27 and 28. Discussions are expected to cover organisational strategy, upcoming Assembly elections and coordination between the Centre, states and the party organisation.The Cabinet meet is also likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's quota, ANI wrote, quoting sources.
Article Summary: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses. The special sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13.

Article Title: 'What is the need for a new Bill?' Congress slams BJP's 'amnesia' on women's Parliament quota
Article Text:
Chidambaram said the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, had already been enacted after the Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament on September 20 and 21, 2023.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday strongly criticised the BJP over its "amnesia" on Women’s Reservation Bill, questioning the delay over its implementation and accusations of the being a roadblock.Congress leader P Chidambaram , targeted Union home minister Amit Shah over his remarks on the issue, saying he was either suffering from "amnesia" or being "economical with the truth".In a post on X, Chidambaram said the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, had already been enacted after the Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament on September 20 and 21, 2023."Congress fully supported the passage of the Bill, and has been demanding the immediate implementation of the Act," he said.Questioning the government's delay, Chidambaram asked: "Why is the BJP government not implementing the Act?""What is the need for a new Bill?" he asked.Congress' general secretary in-charge Communications, Jairam Ramesh, also accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah of misleading the public over the purpose of the special session, alleging that the government was using the issue of women's reservation to divert attention from delimitation."Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying," Ramesh said in a post on X."The Special Session is thus NOT for women’s reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years. The Special Session is for Delimitation," he added.Earlier, Shah said the government was commitment to implementing 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, asserting that Rahul Gandhi would not be able to prevent its implementation.“The women of the country will certainly get 33% reservation of seats in the Parliament and state legislative assemblies,” Shah said. His remarks came ahead of the announcement of a three-day extended special session of Parliament, scheduled from November 30 to December 3."I want to tell Rahul Gandhi that it is our commitment that women of this country will get reservation (in Parliament and Legislative Assemblies). No one will be able to stop us," Shah later said.The Women's Reservation Bill was passed by Parliament in September 2023, providing for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. However, the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, made its implementation conditional on the publication of the first Census conducted after its commencement and a subsequent delimitation exercise to redraw constituencies.In April 2026, the government sought to amend this framework to bring the quota into effect ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Its proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill also sought to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to up to 850 seats and use the 2011 Census for delimitation.However, the Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. The Opposition supported women's reservation but objected to linking it with delimitation.Eight months after the defeat, the government is preparing to revive the proposals in the upcoming extended parliament session.
Article Summary: Congress leader P Chidambaram targeted Union home minister Amit Shah over his remarks on the issue. He said Shah was either suffering from "amnesia" or being "economical with the truth" The Women's Reservation Bill was passed by Parliament in September 2023, providing for 33% reservation for women.

Article Title: DMK 'ready' to support BJP's delimitation bill if Tamil Nadu's representation remains unchanged

CHENNAI: DMK is ready to support the BJP-led Union govt’s proposed delimitation bill if it maintains Tamil Nadu ’s existing percentage of representation and includes a provision for a 25-year freeze, party sources told TOI.It is reliably learned that DMK leadership placed these two demands before the BJP when the latter recently reached out to the Dravidian party.Asked if the party would support a 50% increase in the number of seats across all states from the current strength, a senior DMK leader said, “Yes, with provision built in the bill for a 25-year freeze and maintaining existing representation from all states. Had we not opposed the bill in the past, we could have lost this proposition. If BJP is ready to incorporate these two demands, we have nothing to lose but to gain more in future. ”DMK had opposed delimitation because Tamil Nadu’s representation could be reduced if the 2027 census was used as the basis for the exercise, sources said.“If the new draft bill ensures Tamil Nadu will continue to have the same percentage representation and next delimitation based on the latest census will be carried out only after 25 years, not 100 years as suggested by few, it is a fair deal.It will be beneficial for both DMK as well as Tamil Nadu,” a source said.Asked whether the BJP had recently reached out to DMK, the source said, “Yes, they did and we have given them the demands.”DMK has 22 MPs in Lok Sabha and 8 MPs in Rajya Sabha. The party has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the process to be fair to all sides. In August, DMK backed a resolution of the TVK govt in the assembly urging the Union govt to freeze the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu chief minister, MK Stalin, in a post on X, said, “If the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased, under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s share fall below its current 7.18%! The existing proportion of parliamentary representation among States, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years!”“The DMK remains firm on both these positions today and will continue to do so. The speculation being spread in the media and the grumbling of backstabbers will not shake our position in any way. The DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests,” he added.Meanwhile, CPM state secretary Shanmugam expressed concern over reports that the Union govt had “reached an understanding” with the DMK on the delimitation bill. “On behalf of the CPM, we urge the DMK to remain steadfast in its commitment to protecting the interests of Tamil Nadu and the southern states,” he posted on X.Shanmugam urged the DMK leadership to clarify its stance on delimitation without leaving room for speculation.
Article Summary: DMK has 22 MPs in Lok Sabha and 8 MPs in Rajya Sabha. The party has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the process to be fair to all sides. In August, DMK backed a resolution urging the Union govt to freeze the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.

Article Title: Palamu police bust illicit gun-making unit in Ratnag village, 1 arrested
Article Text:
SDPO Bishrampur Chiranjeev Mandal with the accused at a police station

Daltonganj

:





Palamu police have busted an illicit gun-making unit in Ratnag village under Pandu police station limits after an Arms Act undertrial, taken on police remand, allegedly gave them a lead. Police on Thursday described it as the district’s first such breakthrough in a decade.Police raided the makeshift unit on Nov 25 and arrested 58-year-old Udai Mistri, who allegedly manufactured country-made firearms single-handedly.SDPO Bishrampur Chiranjeev Mandal said, “The unit operated from a shanty located some distance from Mistri’s family home. Police recovered a country-made pistol, trigger and trigger guard, barrel, butt and several partly finished components, besides chisels, files, iron rods, a wrench, hammer and other tools used for making firearms.“Mandal said Mistri had also set up a makeshift furnace to melt and cast metal for manufacturing weapons. Police destroyed the furnace during the raid.The lead came after police took Arms Act undertrial Amit Kumar Singh alias Pappu Singh , 25, of Ratnag, on remand on Nov 24. Police had recovered two country-made pistols from his house on Aug 2, but he had evaded arrest. He surrendered before a court on Nov 5.During interrogation, Pappu allegedly told police that he had purchased the two firearms from Mistri and shared details of his gun-making operation.
Article Summary: Palamu police have busted an illicit gun-making unit in Ratnag village under Pandu police station limits. Police on Thursday described it as the district’s first such breakthrough in a decade. Udai Mistri, 58, allegedly manufactured country-made firearms single-handedly.

Article Title: 98% polling for Solapur DCC, bogus voting accusations by MP
Article Text:
Voting for Solapur DCC bank held on Thursday

Kolhapur





: Around 98% of voters cast their ballots in the election for nine seats of the Solapur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank on Thursday.The five-year tenure of the bank’s board of directors ended in 2024, and the election had been pending since then. Out of the 19 director posts to be filled, 10 candidates—mostly associated with the BJP—were elected unopposed following the withdrawal of nominations. Voting for the remaining nine seats took place on Thursday, with the counting and declaration of results scheduled for Friday.Of the 617 eligible voters, 602 cast their votes via ballot paper. Although 24 candidates were in the fray for the nine posts, the primary contest was between a BJP-led panel and an alliance panel of opposition parties headed by NCP (SP) MP Dhairyashil Mohite-Patil.BJP leader Prashant Paricharak expressed confidence that the BJP would win all nine seats.Meanwhile, Mohite-Patil levelled a serious allegation that pre-stamped ballot papers were brought into the Sangola polling booth and dropped into the ballot box.“Candidates Aniket Deshmukh and Sanjay Ingole have filed a complaint in this regard with the polling officer,” the MP said, adding that he had written to the returning officer requesting CCTV footage to verify the claims and take further action.“Some people are stealing ballot papers. I have sought the CCTV footage from the voting period and demanded action against the booth officer, who initially refused to accept the complaint, as well as the police on duty for failing to stop bogus voting. If we do not get satisfactory answers, we will approach the appropriate court,” Mohite-Patil said.
Article Summary: Around 98% of voters cast their ballots in the election for nine seats of the Solapur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank on Thursday. The five-year tenure of the bank’s board of directors ended in 2024, and the election had been pending since then. Of the 617 eligible voters, 602 cast their votes via ballot paper.

Article Title: 50-year-old man accused of spiking woman's drink, raping her at Belapur lodge

NAVI MUMBAI: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist.Dwivedi was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha and four others of Rs 19 lakh in a flat sale deal. After she felt dizzy, he took her to Arush Lodge and sexually assaulted her.She further alleged that Dwivedi threatened to kill her and her family if she disclosed the incident to anyone. He also threatened to circulate an intimate video, which he had allegedly recorded on his mobile phone.Pawar said, "The woman claimed that she did not approach the police earlier because of Dwivedi's threats.After learning that he had been arrested in another case and lodged in jail, she came forward and registered an FIR against him."Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to rape, administering stupefying or intoxicating substances, aggravated criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of public peace.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme Court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist. Article Title: Lawyers seeks CBI probe into pvt schools recognition scam involving Anbil Mahesh
Article Text:
Chennai:





A lawyer has moved Madras high court seeking a CBI probe into the alleged ₹100 crore private schools recognition cheating case involving former school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi.The petitioner advocate K Venkatachalapathy claimed that the alleged scam requires a probe by Central Bureau of Investigation in view of the statements made by the state finance minister N Marie Wilson in the assembly floor. Wilson said he was forced to pay a bribe to the school education department during the previous DMK govt to get approvals for his educational institutions at T Nagar, Chennai.“The statements made by the minister require an independent and comprehensive investigation, particularly with regard to the identity of the person who demanded and received the money, the institutions concerned,” the petitioner said.Former minister Anbil Mahesh countered the statement and alleged that the institutions of Wilson were facing certain violations. Such allegations must also be independently probed to ascertain whether any preferential govt approval has been given to the institutions of the finance minister, he said.The plea moved as a PIL is likely to be taken up for hearing by the first bench headed by the Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari next week.
Article Summary: A lawyer has moved Madras high court seeking a CBI probe into the alleged private schools recognition cheating case involving former school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi. The plea moved as a PIL is likely to be taken up for hearing by the first bench headed by the Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari.

Article Title: Sulur minor girl rape and murder case: Coimbatore court convicts two accused, to pronounce quantum of sentence on Dec 4
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A special court for POCSO cases in Coimbatore on Friday found two men guilty in the rape and murder of a minor girl in Sulur in May this year. Judge K Hariharan will pronounce the quantum of sentence against the convicts, K Karthi and R Mohan, on Dec 4.On May 21, the 10-year-old girl went missing after going to a nearby grocery shop in Pallapalayam. Sulur police launched a search operation after her parents lodged a complaint. On May 22, police recovered her body from an isolated spot near the Kannampalayam lakebed.Police arrested Karthi, 35, and Mohan, 31, both construction workers residing in the same locality, in connection with the crime.The first accused, Karthi, was charged under sections 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4), 103(1), 238(a), 127(2) and 65(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), read with sections 5(l), 5(l), 5(m) and 5(j)(iv), read with Section 6(1) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.Second accused Mohan was charged under sections 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4) read with sections 49, 238(a), 240 and 249(a) of the BNS, read with sections 6(1) 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act Police filed an 819-page chargesheet before the special court on June 10, less than three weeks after recovering the girl's body.The trial commenced on June 24. During the proceedings, the court examined 68 witnesses and recorded 221 documents as evidence.The verdict was initially scheduled for Nov 16 but was subsequently postponed to Nov 27.Amid tight police security, Karthik and Mohan were brought to the POCSO special court on Friday ahead of the pronouncement of the verdict.While being escorted to the court, Mohan addressed reporters and said, “I was the one who helped police nab Karthik. Please do not call me his friend. It is wrong to describe me his friend. Karthik was in contact with the women in my family. I have committed no offence and have nothing to do with this case. I will convey the same to the judge as well,” he said.
Article Summary: The 10-year-old girl went missing after going to a nearby grocery shop in Pallapalayam. Sulur police launched a search operation after her parents lodged a complaint. On May 22, police recovered her body from an isolated spot near the Kannampalayan lakebed.

Article Title: Tirupur farmers hold protest seeking full waiver of cooperative crop loans
Article Text: TIRUPUR: More than 100 farmers held a protest in front of the Tirupur district collectorate condemning state govt for not fully waiving cooperative crop loans. They urged govt to implement the complete waiver promised during the elections.The agitation was led by N Ramesh, Tirupur city and district secretary of Tamil Nadu Farmers Protection Association. He said chief minister C Joseph Vijay, during the poll campaign, had assured that cooperative crop loans would be waived fully for farmers owning under five acres and by 50% for those owning above five acres, without conditions, calling it a “guarantee.”Ramesh said Tamil Nadu’s farmers had availed cooperative crop loans of around Rs 20,000 crore, but govt initially announced only Rs 2,000 crore in the first phase, triggering widespread disappointment. Following sustained protests by farmers and farm bodies, the relief ceiling for beneficiaries was raised, with the amount increased to Rs 35,000 from an earlier Rs 5,000 for farmers with loans above Rs 1 lakh, he said.He added that more than 50 farmers’ organisations had formed a federation and held continuous sit-in protests. Later, during talks in Chennai, it was announced that Rs 75,000 would be provided to all, he said.However, farmers alleged that multiple conditions remained and those who took crop loans during 2022, 2023, 2024 and in Jan-April 2025 were left out. With monsoon failure linked to El Nino and worsening drought, they said repayment is impossible and fresh loans are unavailable. Farmers submitted petitions to the district collector and the joint registrar of cooperatives.
Article Summary: More than 100 farmers held a protest in front of the Tirupur district collectorate condemning state govt for not fully waiving cooperative crop loans. They urged govt to implement the complete waiver promised during the elections. The agitation was led by N Ramesh, Tir upur city and district secretary of Tamil Nadu Farmers Protection Association.

Article Title: Land surveyor, middleman booked for accepting bribe near Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against a land surveyor and a middleman in Sulur for accepting a bribe of Rs 25,000 to survey a parcel of land and facilitate the issuance of a separate patta.The accused have been identified as Balamurugan, 35, a govt-licensed land surveyor attached to the Sulur taluk office, and Praveenkumar, 32, who runs an e-service centre in the area.According to DVAC officials, Arun Kumar, a milk trader from Pollachi, owns a piece of land at Kalangal near Sulur. He approached Balamurugan in late August to survey the property and provide the necessary documents for obtaining a separate patta. Balamurugan demanded Rs 20,000 to survey the property and recommend to the tahsildar the issuance of a separate patta. Unwilling to pay the bribe, Arun Kumar lodged a complaint with the chief minister’s special cell.After learning about the complaint, Balamurugan increased the demand by Rs 5,000 and insisted that Arun Kumar pay Rs 25,000. He allegedly instructed him to transfer the money through GPay to Praveenkumar, the middleman.Arun Kumar transferred the amount, following which the property was surveyed, and the documents were handed over to him.Arun Kumar subsequently informed the Coimbatore DVAC officials about the bribery. After obtaining govt permission, the DVAC registered a case under the Prevention of Corruption Act against both men on Tuesday. Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against a land surveyor and a middleman in Sulur. The accused have been identified as Balamurugan, 35, and Praveenkumar, 32, who runs an e-service centre in the area.

Article Title: Man held for damaging two Karunanidhi statues, glass panels of DMK library and office in Erode
Article Text:
The Erode district police launched an intensive investigation and examined CCTV footage. The footage revealed that the same man had visited the various locations and caused the damage.





ERODE: The Erode district police on Tuesday arrested a man on charges of damaging two statues of late Tamil Nadu chief minister M Karunanidhi , a library and a DMK party office.The incidents came to light after the spectacles on the Karunanidhi statue at Panneerselvam Park in Erode were found broken. The Karunanidhi statue at Alangattu Valasu in Modakkurichi was also damaged.“The glass panels of a library situated beneath Karunanidhi’s statue in the Municipal Colony area were damaged. In another incident, the front glass facade of the DMK district headquarters at Manalmedu was found shattered,” said a party functionary.The Erode district police launched an intensive investigation and examined CCTV footage. The footage revealed that the same man had visited the various locations and caused the damage.“Based on the investigation, police identified the suspect as Hari Vignesh, 26, of Thottipalayam Pudur near Modakkurichi,” said superintendent of police D V Kiran Shruthi. The man, who was drunk on Monday night, also damaged the doors and window panes of his own house as well as the windows of some vehicles.Police said legal action would be initiated. Preliminary inquiries indicated that the man might be suffering from mental health-related issues.
Article Summary: The incidents came to light after the spectacles on the Karunanidhi statue at Panneerselvam Park in Erode were found broken. The glass panels of a library situated beneath the statue were also damaged. The front glass facade of the DMK district headquarters at Manalmedu was found shattered.

A man was arrested on Thursday for allegedly attacking a woman with scissors after she opposed his alleged pressure to convert and plan to marry another woman. The accused was arrested near COD bridge in Kanpur by Railbazar police.The woman, a resident of Kanpur, alleged in her complaint that the accused married her at a temple about five years ago and took her to Noida. She alleged that the accused then called her back to Kanpur on the false assurance that he would perform nikah with her and accommodate her at his parents’ house. After arriving, she learnt that he was preparing to marry another woman.When she opposed the proposed marriage and refused to convert despite alleged pressure from Kaleem and his family, he attacked her neck with scissors with the intention of killing her, according to the complaint. He subsequently fled.Acting station house officer Ashish Chaubey said police registered a case under relevant sections based on the woman’s written complaint.During questioning, the accused admitted that he was attempting to flee to Noida. He was produced before a court and sent to jail.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Govt school teacher arrested under POCSO Act in Salem district
Article Text:

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district. He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’

Article Title: Pedestrian fatally hit by truck in Aluva
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A pedestrian was killed after being hit by a truck while crossing the road near Metro pillar 111 at Companypady in Aluva around 8am on Thursday.Shaikh Ahmed Ali Jalaluddin, 61, of Keezhmadu, Aluva, is the deceased. The truck was heading towards Ernakulam from Aluva. Jalaluddin, who suffered grievous injuries, was rushed to Aluva Govt Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.The Aluva police registered a case for rash driving and causing death by negligence based on the victim’s son’s statement. The police said that an investigation has been launched to find how exactly the accident occurred. The body was handed over to his relatives after an autopsy.
Article Summary: Shaikh Ahmed Ali Jalaluddin, 61, of Keezhmadu, Aluva, is the deceased. He suffered grievous injuries and died in hospital. Police have registered a case for rash driving and causing death by negligence.
